claims.text: A thin nitride interlayer between zirconium-alloy cladding and an elemental Cr coating will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The nitride interlayer will act as an effective diffusion barrier.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the oxidation-protective integrity of the Cr coating in subcritical water.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the oxidation-protective integrity of the Cr coating in high-temperature steam.
The unmodified elemental Cr coating suffers interdiffusion-induced degradation under combined service conditions.
A nanoscale conformal CrN interlayer can be deposited on the zirconium-alloy surface before application of the elemental Cr coating.
The proposed interlayer will remain continuous and well adhered during the specified exposures.
The nitride interlayer will limit atomic migration across the Zr-substrate/Cr-coating interface.
The nitride barrier reduces the interfacial diffusivity of both Cr and Zr atoms.
Reduced Cr and Zr diffusivity will mitigate formation of deleterious intermetallic compounds.
Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds compromise coating integrity.
The CrN interlayer will preserve the oxidation resistance of the outer Cr layer.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the modified coating will show less interfacial Cr–Zr diffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the modified coating will form fewer intermetallic phases.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the modified coating will have improved mechanical integrity.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the modified coating will sustain oxidation protection during long-term exposure to subcritical water at 300–360°C.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the modified coating will sustain oxidation protection during short steam transients up to approximately 1200°C.
The unmodified Cr coating fails prematurely under combined thermal exposures because of interdiffusion at the coating–substrate interface.
Laboratory-scale evidence indicates that nanolayer nitride barriers reduce interdiffusion.
The effectiveness of the proposed interlayer under high neutron irradiation is unknown.
